assumptions.condition: The potential-outcome array \(Y\) is fixed under the randomization law.

standard.name: One-sided uniform overlap for the nonrare arm

novel.justification: A prespecified critical allocation schedule can fix its initial exploration mass, as in clipped inverse-time exploration rules.
Bounded positive intensity profiles include inverse-time exploration, late ramps, and affine exploration floors used in adaptive allocation.
Daily or batched allocation probabilities generated from clipped smooth scores have piecewise-Lipschitz expected intensity trajectories.
Bounded outcomes and bounded prespecified endpoint predictions imply a bounded residual trajectory.
A prespecified expected-endpoint bridge under gradual calendar drift yields a uniformly continuous residual trajectory with an auditable modulus.

The contract is checkable for adaptive rules with a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge and deterministic uniform moduli; it makes the approximation target fixed before the assignment path is realized.

assumptions.condition: Every numerical input to \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) and \(\mathsf{FastCert}_n\) is rational or is supplied with a certified rational interval enclosure.

novel.justification: Logged probabilities and trial protocol constants are stored at finite precision, and elementary logarithms admit directed rational interval evaluation.

definitions.name: Critical intensity class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q=\{q':[0,1]\to\mathbb R:q'(0)=c,\ c/2\le q'(u)\le K,\ |q'(u)-q'(v)|\le L_q|u-v|\text{ for all }u,v\in[0,1]\}\)

definitions.name: Signed residual class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R=\{r':[0,1]\to\mathbb R:|r'(u)|\le B,\ |r'(u)-r'(v)|\le L_r|u-v|\text{ for all }u,v\in[0,1]\}\)

definitions.name: Completed-log profile enclosure
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_n(e)=\{q'\in\mathcal Q:|q'(t/n)-t e_{nt}|\le\delta_{q,n}\text{ for every }t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\}\), represented by rational outer boxes satisfying the pointwise and adjacent Lipschitz constraints.

definitions.name: Stopped finite-transfer budget
definitions.construction: Use \(T_n,\ell_n,H_{1,n},H_{2,n},L_j,D_{\mathrm{mark},n},I_{\mathrm{grid},n},D_{\mathrm{grid},n},v_{E,n},v_{C,n},v_{Z,n}\) exactly as declared in the symbol table and set \(D_{\mathrm{tr},n}=\kappa_n+\delta_{q,n}H_{1,n}+2K^2H_{2,n}+I_{\mathrm{grid},n}+(D_{\mathrm{mark},n}+D_{\mathrm{grid},n})/h_n+(v_{E,n}+v_{C,n}+v_{Z,n})/h_n^2\).

definitions.name: Directed-rational logged-profile certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) enumerates rational Lipschitz outer boxes for \(\mathcal Q_n(e)\) and \(\mathcal R\), truncates the Poisson integral near zero with a rational cutoff and a Campbell bound, quantizes time and signed jumps with the common-Poisson Wasserstein bound, truncates the total count with a certified Poisson-tail bound, performs direct directed-rational signed-mark convolution, adds net, quadrature, count, and rounding allowances totaling at most \(\zeta_n\), and returns the smallest rational \(a_n\) whose certificate proves \(\sup_{q'\in\mathcal Q_n(e),r'\in\mathcal R}\mathbb E H_{a_n,h_n}(Z_{r',q'})\le\alpha-\Delta_n\); if \(T_n\le K\), \(\delta_{q,n}>c/4\), the enclosure is empty, or \(\Delta_n\ge\alpha\), it returns the full-range flag.

definitions.name: Certified critical interval
definitions.construction: If \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) returns \(a_n\), set \(b_n=a_n+4h_n\) and \(C_n=[\widehat\tau_n-b_n-h_n,\widehat\tau_n+b_n+h_n]\cap[-2M,2M]\); otherwise set \(C_n=[-2M,2M]\).

definitions.name: Exact late-ramp pair
definitions.construction: At \(c=a_0=1/2\) and \(\delta_0=1/4\), for \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) set \(\bar q^{\sigma}(u)=c\), \(r^{\sigma}(u)=\sigma\delta_0(u-a_0)_+/(1-a_0)\), \(e_{nt}=c/t\), \(m_{nt}(a)=0\), \(Y_{nt}(0)=0\), and \(Y_{nt}^{\sigma}(1)=r^{\sigma}(t/n)\); take \(M\ge\delta_0\), \(\rho\ge c\), \(K\ge c\), and \(L_r\ge\delta_0/(1-a_0)\), and let the complete observation be \(O_n\).

definitions.name: Branch-and-bound certificate handle
definitions.construction: Work in the deterministic multitape Turing bit model. The input consists of \(n\), the rational log \(e_{n1:n}\), rational outer-enclosure endpoints and protocol constants, \(\alpha\), and \(\xi\), with total binary length \(\Lambda_n\). For every profile-box node \(V\), maintain directed-rational bounds \(L(V)\le\sup_{(q',r')\in V}\mathbb E H_{b,h_n}(Z_{r',q'})\le U(V)\) and the invariant \(U(V)-L(V)\le h_n^{-1}[(2K/c+1)\operatorname{diam}_r(V)+(4KB/c^2+2B/c)\operatorname{diam}_q(V)]+\epsilon_{\mathrm{conv}}(V)\), where the outward convolution error \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{conv}}(V)\) is charged to the remaining rational budget. Prune \(V\) when \(U(V)\le\alpha-\Delta_n\), reject the trial threshold when \(L(V)>\alpha-\Delta_n\), and bisect only boxes whose certified interval straddles \(\alpha-\Delta_n\). The target \(\mathsf{FastCert}_n(e,\alpha,\xi)\) is an outward-valid threshold \(\widetilde a_n\) within \(\xi\) of the exhaustive certificate threshold.

statements.statement: On \(G_n\), the true intensity profile \(\bar q\) belongs to the completed-log enclosure \(\mathcal Q_n(e)\). Moreover, every \(q'\in\mathcal Q_n(e)\) satisfies \(\|q'-\bar q\|_{\infty}\le d_{Q,n}=2\delta_{q,n}+2L_q(\varepsilon_n+1/n)\).
statements.justification: This converts the completed propensity log into a simultaneous deterministic enclosure without conditioning away assignment dependence.
statements.gap: FreidlingZhaoGao2026 uses exact selection-event conditioning; no located result supplies a shrinking Lipschitz intensity enclosure for an approximate critical law.
statements.consumer: The deterministic inclusion is the selection-safety input for the certified radius used in the GUSTO-1 and EUROPA bridge analysis.

statements.statement: For every \(n\), the directed-dyadic bandwidth satisfies \(x_n\le h_n\le x_n+2^{-n}\). Uniformly over the declared class, \(x_n\to0\) and hence \(h_n\to0\). In particular, \(0\le5(h_n-x_n)\le5\cdot2^{-n}\), so dyadic rounding inflates the reported radius \(a_n+5h_n\) by at most \(5\cdot2^{-n}\) relative to \(a_n+5x_n\).
statements.justification: The explicit dyadic bracket makes the smoothing choice effective and isolates its finite numerical contribution to interval radius.
statements.gap: The nearby adaptive-inference results do not track directed rounding of an atom-safe smoothing bandwidth through an oracle-radius comparison.
statements.consumer: The coverage theorem and clinical-log implementation receive an auditable \(5\cdot2^{-n}\) radius charge rather than an unspecified approximation error.

statements.statement: For every \(n\) with \(T_n>K\) and \(\delta_{q,n}\le c/4\), there is an extension of the randomization probability space carrying \(Z_{r,\bar q}\) such that \(\Pr(G_n^c\cup\{|S_n-Z_{r,\bar q}|>4h_n\})\le D_{\mathrm{tr},n}\), where every term of \(D_{\mathrm{tr},n}\) is the declared computable budget and \(D_{\mathrm{tr},n}\to0\) uniformly over all experiments satisfying the declared assumptions.
statements.justification: The explicit stopped coupling is the theorem-level bridge from adaptive finite experiments to an atomic signed critical law.
statements.gap: LiZhao2026 derives a martingale CLT under Lindeberg, while BarbourXia1999 treats integer-valued compound-Poisson approximation; neither covers predictable stopping with real signed residual marks and this finite error allocation.
statements.consumer: Any fixed-horizon adaptive trial whose logged probabilities and expected-endpoint bridge satisfy the declared moduli receives an auditable non-Gaussian calibration error.

statements.statement: For \(q,q'\in\mathcal Q\) and \(r,r'\in\mathcal R\), a common Poisson construction satisfies \(W_1(\mathcal L(Z_{r,q}),\mathcal L(Z_{r',q'}))\le(2K/c+1)\|r-r'\|_{\infty}+(4KB/c^2+2B/c)\|q-q'\|_{\infty}\); consequently the corresponding ramp risks differ by at most this bound divided by \(h_n\).
statements.justification: This quantitative continuity makes exhaustive profile nets and directed convolution a finite certificate rather than a compactness assertion.
statements.gap: Classical compound-Poisson Stein bounds do not provide this near-zero real signed-mark profile metric in the logged adaptive calibration problem.
statements.consumer: The bound allocates profile discretization error and yields a terminating certification mesh.

statements.statement: The algorithm \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) terminates for every certified input. Uniformly over all experiments satisfying the declared assumptions, the reported interval obeys \(\Pr(\tau_n\in C_n)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\), where infeasible budgets trigger \([-2M,2M]\). Moreover, for every \(\eta\in(0,\alpha)\) and \(s>0\), uniformly over the fixed compact profile classes, on \(G_n\) and for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(b_{\alpha}(\bar q)\le b_n+h_n\le b_{\alpha-\eta}(\bar q)+s+5\cdot2^{-n}\). The last term is the complete radius charge for replacing \(x_n\) by its directed-dyadic upper bracket \(h_n\). This covers the declared \(e_{nt}\asymp\bar q(t/n)/t\) profiles that fall outside the Lindeberg condition used for Gaussian coverage in LiZhao2026, Theorem 4(ii).
statements.justification: This is the main inferential claim: computable finite-experiment validity, same-log selection safety, and profile-adaptive radius control all survive atoms.
statements.gap: WaudbySmithEtAl2024 gives generic martingale validity and ChoBibautKallus2025 gives asymptotic simulation inversion, but neither gives a completed-log atomic profile certificate with oracle level and radius slack.
statements.consumer: LiberaliEtAl2025's delayed-endpoint RTAR analysis can use the interval conditional on a prespecified bridge that verifies the declared moduli.

statements.statement: For each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), the exact late-ramp construction satisfies the declared fixed-outcome, boundedness, predictable-randomization, intensity-profile, residual-profile, and profile-contract conditions for all sufficiently large \(n\). In particular, \(\bar q^{\sigma}\in\mathcal Q\), \(r^{\sigma}\in\mathcal R\), the profile errors vanish, the early rare-arm quadratic variation is eventually zero, and \(\tau_n^{+}-\tau_n^{-}\ge1/8\).
statements.justification: The least-favorable witness must be shown to lie in the same declared adaptive class before it can support a uniform information bound.
statements.gap: Existing adaptive-width lower bounds do not verify membership of this exact finite-population late-ramp pair with a completed propensity log.
statements.consumer: The membership certificate makes the numerical lower-bound constant auditable against the proposal's maintained class.

statements.statement: For the exact late-ramp pair and every possibly randomized confidence set \(D_n\) measurable from \(O_n\), if \(\liminf_n\min_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}\Pr_{\sigma}(\tau_n^{\sigma}\in D_n)\ge0.95\), then for each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), \(\liminf_n\Pr_{\sigma}(\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge1/8)\ge\sqrt{1/2}-0.1=0.6071067811865475\ldots\).
statements.justification: The theorem establishes an information bound for every honest confidence set from the complete logged experiment, not an estimator-specific implication of the HT limit.
statements.gap: ShekharRamdas2023 treats i.i.d. bounded-mean width and HongLeungLi2020 treats diverging effective information; neither uses a shared adaptive void event with this exact finite-population constant.
statements.consumer: Trial designers obtain a quantitative warning that nominally valid inference cannot be uniformly narrow when an arm receives only bounded cumulative allocation hazard.

statements.statement: For every \(n\) divisible by \(32\) in the exact late-ramp pair, the HT-centered interval of error radius \(13/32\) has coverage at least \(1-0.03794\) under both signs. A \(16\)-cell directed-rational compound-Poisson envelope certifies the sharper ramp-risk bound \(0.0379330711865835\).
statements.justification: This exact finite calculation is the early kill test for atom handling, signed profiles, and threshold padding.
statements.gap: No cited adaptive-inference paper supplies a reproducible directed-integer certificate for this atomic rare-arm ramp law.
statements.consumer: The certificate is a regression test for the general convolution implementation before it is trusted on clinical logs.

statements.statement: For each \(r\in\mathcal R\), the affine high-hazard construction satisfies the declared assumptions for all sufficiently large \(n\): \(\bar q_H\in\mathcal Q\), the profile errors vanish after the cutoff, and its deterministic early rare-arm quadratic-variation envelope is \(O(M^2\varepsilon_n^2+M^2/n)\).
statements.justification: The favorable subclass must be legal under the same primitive design and profile requirements used by the coverage theorem.
statements.gap: No cited result verifies an affine critical-hazard finite-population subclass with an explicit vanishing early-variation envelope.
statements.consumer: The membership result prevents the \(0.442M\) comparison from relying on an oracle or inadmissible subclass.

statements.statement: On the affine high-hazard subfamily, \(\sup_{r\in\mathcal R}\operatorname{Var}(Z_{r,\bar q_H})\le M^2[100-(1/2)\log(201)]/10000<0.009735M^2\), so \(b_{0.05}(\bar q_H)\le0.442M\). Consequently the certified interval has radius at most \(0.442M+s+5\cdot2^{-n}\) on \(G_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), for every \(s>0\).
statements.justification: The strict numerical upper bound shows that profile adaptation delivers a nonvacuous width gain on a legal subclass without assuming observed rare marks reveal all counterfactual residuals.
statements.gap: CookMishlerRamdas2024 studies truncation empirically and asymptotically, but does not certify a robust atomic radius over unknown signed residual profiles.
statements.consumer: An adaptive trial with a prespecified affine exploration floor receives an explicit conservative radius benchmark.

statements.statement: In the homogeneous-residual special case \(\bar q(u)\equiv c\) and \(r(u)\equiv r(0)\), the raw jump sum underlying \(Z_{r,\bar q}\), after the declared centering and scaling, is the generalized Dickman law with parameter \(c\) studied by BhattacharjeeGoldstein2019. If \(r(0)=0\), then \(Z_{r,\bar q}=0\) and the finite-transfer inequality specializes to \(\Pr(G_n^c\cup\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|>4h_n\})\le D_{\mathrm{tr},n}\).
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the new profile law agrees with a known limit under homogeneous residuals rather than renaming the Dickman distribution.
statements.gap: BhattacharjeeGoldstein2019 settles the homogeneous weighted-sum limit; the present novelty begins with signed heterogeneous profiles, adaptive transfer, and inference.
statements.consumer: Readers can validate the calibration code against a known one-parameter law before using general profiles.

statements.statement: In the deterministic multitape Turing bit model, can \(\mathsf{FastCert}_n(e,\alpha,\xi)\) be constructed so that, for fixed \(c,K,L_q,L_r,B\), its bit complexity is bounded by a polynomial in \(n\), the total input length \(\Lambda_n\), and \(\xi^{-1}\)? On every feasible input for which \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) returns \(a_n\), it must terminate with \(\widetilde a_n\) satisfying \(a_n\le\widetilde a_n\le a_n+\xi\) and \(\sup_{q'\in\mathcal Q_n(e),r'\in\mathcal R}\mathbb E H_{\widetilde a_n,h_n}(Z_{r',q'})\le\alpha-\Delta_n\). Can this be achieved with the certified pruning invariant in the branch-and-bound handle while retaining the \(13/32\) late-ramp certificate and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard oracle bound, with only \(\xi\) added to a reported computational radius?
statements.justification: The exhaustive certificate establishes computability but may be expensive; a complexity-controlled certificate is the first-class unresolved computational-statistical question.
statements.gap: Neither classical compound-Poisson approximation nor selective randomization inference gives a polynomial-time outward-rounded optimization over continuous signed profile classes.
statements.consumer: A polynomial certificate would make prespecified daily calibration feasible at the GUSTO-1 and EUROPA trial scales.

sampling_model.design: A triangular array of binary sequential experiments with fixed finite-population potential outcomes and assignment as the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Given \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\), \(A_{nt}\) is Bernoulli with known logged predictable probability \(e_{nt}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The rare-arm probability follows \(t e_{nt}\approx \bar q(t/n)\) after an early cutoff, with bounded cumulative hazard and \(0<e_{nt}\le\rho<1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Predictable regressions \(m_{nt}(a)\) may be arbitrary within their bound; their treated residuals follow a deterministic Lipschitz profile on one common high-probability event.
sampling_model.randomness: Only the known adaptive randomization law is random; there is no superpopulation sampling assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: If Condition 3 holds, the standardized AIPW estimator converges in distribution to a standard normal law.
Theorem 1 constructs doubly robust betting confidence sequences under predictable logging.
Proposition 1 proves selective type-I error control for the selective randomization p-value.
Theorem 1 proves asymptotic type-I error control for simulation with optimism in specified adaptive designs.
Proposition 2 gives an exact compound-Poisson law for an HT rate estimator under independent Poisson importance sampling.
Finite-population limited-overlap estimators are asymptotically Gaussian when their effective sample size diverges.
Any valid i.i.d. bounded-mean confidence interval obeys an inverse-information-projection width lower bound.
Stein perturbation yields explicit total-variation compound-Poisson approximation bounds for integer-valued sums.
Weighted Bernoulli and Poisson sums admit generalized Dickman approximation bounds.
Theorem 1 gives a semiparametrically efficient Gaussian limit for the truncated A2IPW estimator.
Resampling simulations find tighter superior-arm and wider inferior-arm intervals under real-time adaptive randomization.

tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, where the cumulative allocation hazard is bounded, the finite-population AIPW error is not generically Gaussian. The project constructs a stopped coupling from the adaptive assignment process to an independent Bernoulli array and then to a signed marked Poisson integral, with an explicit finite-experiment error budget. A directed-rational profile-net convolution calibrates an atom-safe confidence interval from the completed propensity log using an explicit dyadic bandwidth bracket whose radius charge is at most \(5\cdot2^{-n}\). The main theorem gives uniform randomization coverage and an oracle radius inequality with explicit level and radius slack. A separate complete-experiment void-event argument shows that every \(95\%\)-honest confidence set has diameter at least \(1/8\) with limiting probability at least \(0.60710678\) on an exact late-ramp pair, while a legal high-hazard subfamily has robust limiting radius at most \(0.442M\) apart from the declared slack and dyadic charge.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao establish design-based Gaussian AIPW inference under variance-convergence and Lindeberg conditions, and Waudby-Smith et al. establish generic anytime-valid martingale intervals under predictable logging. Neither result calibrates the discontinuous signed compound-Poisson law that remains when rare-arm cumulative hazard is bounded, nor does either derive an all-confidence-set width obstruction from the complete logged experiment.
project_justification.niche: The bounded-hazard boundary is statistically distinct: only finitely many informative rare assignments survive in the limit, atoms cannot be handled by routine quantile convergence, and a threshold selected from the completed propensity log must be protected against same-log selection.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a computable adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer, a simultaneous profile enclosure and directed convolution certificate, an explicit directed-dyadic bandwidth with a vanishing radius charge, an atom-safe coverage and oracle-radius theorem, and a separate void-event lower bound for arbitrary confidence sets.

related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest setup and writing model: fixed potential outcomes, adaptive assignment as the only randomness, and an AIPW martingale decomposition. Their Condition 3 and Theorem 4 deliver Gaussian inference only after variance convergence and Lindeberg, whereas the present critical profiles retain order-one rare-arm increments. Bibaut and Kallus (2024) organize adaptive inference into martingale-CLT repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws; their review identifies the last route as incomplete beyond special settings. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) provide exact predictable-logging martingale confidence sequences without a global importance-weight bound; their generic boundaries inform the safety architecture but do not determine the signed atomic profile radius. Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026) condition exact randomization tests on adaptive selection; the present calibration instead uses deterministic threshold domination because conditioning on the completed propensity log cannot create an independent Bernoulli reference. Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) invert simulated nonnormal adaptive laws under stochastic bandit models; the proposed interval is design-based and uses certified outward error rather than Monte Carlo approximation. Chen et al. (2026) derive an exact compound-Poisson HT rate model under independent Poisson importance sampling and propose monotone bootstrap intervals; their result neither treats a signed causal contrast under adaptive assignment nor supplies uniform finite-experiment coverage. Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat finite-population limited overlap in a diverging-effective-information regime. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) derive i.i.d. bounded-mean width lower bounds; the proposed lower bound acts on the complete sequential experiment through its shared void atom. Barbour and Xia (1999) motivate explicit coupling and Stein error accounting for compound-Poisson approximation, while Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the constant-profile Dickman reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) are the applied consumer: their delayed-endpoint GUSTO-1 and EUROPA simulations document inferior-arm interval inflation but do not prove conditional finite-population coverage.
technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete statistical experiments. It cannot by itself imply an information bound for arbitrary estimators; Theorem \(\mathrm{7}\) therefore uses a separate shared-subprobability argument. The deterministic profiles are fixed before the path is realized. A claim that a suitable profile exists only after observing outcomes would invalidate the threshold comparison. Exact no-slack quantile convergence is not asserted at atoms. The high-hazard result is an upper bound on a declared subfamily, not a globally sharp minimax-width constant.
honest_scope: The open core is the independently checked end-to-end proof and implementation of the stopped coupling, rational profile enclosure, signed convolution, and deterministic threshold allocation over the full declared class. The directed-dyadic bandwidth is explicit and vanishes, with a reported-radius charge bounded by \(5\cdot2^{-n}\). The separate computational question asks for polynomial bit complexity in \(n\), total rational input length \(\Lambda_n\), and \(\xi^{-1}\) under the stated certified pruning invariant. The \(16\)-bin ramp computation and high-hazard Chebyshev arithmetic are reproducible diagnostics, not substitutes for the uniform theorem. The application to Liberali et al. is conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge that verifies the deterministic profile and modulus contract. Random profile or Cox-process extensions, exact atom-free quantile claims, and globally optimal expected-width constants are outside scope. Under the homogeneous-residual constant-intensity special case, the law reduces to the known generalized Dickman result in Proposition \(\mathrm{11}\).

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Section 2, Condition 3, Theorem 4, the proof in Supplement S2.3, the vanishing-probability simulation in Section 6.3, and the Discussion. The proof writes AIPW error as a martingale array and invokes variance convergence plus Lindeberg; the first changed step at \(e_{nt}\asymp 1/t\) is to replace the martingale CLT by stopped Bernoulli coupling and marked-Poisson transfer.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct an atom-safe, finite-error confidence interval and pair it with an all-procedure honest-width frontier in the bounded-hazard design-based experiment.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Uniformly couple \(S_n\) to \(Z_{r,\bar q}\) with a computable error budget, certify same-log critical radii over profile nets, prove uniform coverage and oracle slack, and separately prove the exact late-ramp diameter lower bound and high-hazard upper radius.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Li and Zhao's martingale Lindeberg verification fails because a single rare-arm inverse-propensity increment remains order one; stop at envelope violations and couple the remaining predictable Bernoulli draws to independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\bar q(t/n)/t)\) draws.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining adaptive finite-population inference, bounded cumulative hazard, compound-Poisson confidence intervals, signed marks, and logged propensity calibration found LiZhao2026, WaudbySmithEtAl2024, ChoBibautKallus2025, and classical Poisson approximation, but no theorem containing this target-method pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from LiZhao2026 because their design-based AIPW theorem already permits vanishing propensities.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their Theorem 4(ii) is Gaussian only under Condition 3, whose Lindeberg term excludes order-one critical increments; their Section 6.3 documents failure as probabilities decay faster, and it supplies neither an atomic critical-law calibration nor an all-set lower bound.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Proposition 1 and its conditional-randomization construction, Supplement S2, and the Discussion. Their selection protection conditions on assignments that reproduce the same design choice; the first changed step is to replace exact conditional randomization simulation by simultaneous outward-rounded bounds for an approximate atomic law.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove that a profile-net index chosen from the same completed propensity log can be used for calibration without conditioning on that log as if assignments became independent.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A deterministic monotone-threshold lemma turns simultaneous profile enclosures into selection-safe unconditional coverage and an oracle radius inequality at atoms.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace equality of the conditional randomization kernel after selection by a pathwise inclusion between the selected threshold and the deterministic robust threshold of the true profile.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for selective randomization with compound-Poisson calibration or certified profile nets returned FreidlingZhaoGao2026 and generic martingale methods, but no deterministic atom-safe enclosure theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from selective randomization inference because choosing a profile is just another selection event.
seed_details.rebuttal: The exact conditional randomization law is not available after adaptive-to-Poisson approximation, and conditioning on the completed propensity log does not yield independent assignments; the required proof is a simultaneous deterministic enclosure plus threshold monotonicity argument.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Theorem 1 and its martingale-CLT proof outline, the truncation experiment in Section 4.3, and the Conclusion. The paper explicitly identifies finite-time truncation and confidence-set width as open directions; the first changed step is to compare complete sequential logged experiments through their shared no-rare-assignment submeasure rather than to analyze one A2IPW statistic.
seed_details.opportunity: Determine a non-Gaussian honest-diameter adaptation obstruction over late-ramp laws and contrast it with a high-hazard profile class.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For an exact \(c=a=1/2\), \(\delta=1/4\) pair, every \(95\%\)-honest confidence set has diameter at least \(1/8\) with limiting probability at least \(\sqrt{1/2}-0.1\); a separate certified interval has robust high-hazard radius at most \(0.442M\) plus slack.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace semiparametric influence-function or estimator-width analysis by a common-subprobability argument for the full assignment, propensity, and outcome observation.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent searches found ShekharRamdas2023 for i.i.d. bounded means and HongLeungLi2020 for diverging effective sample size, but no adaptive finite-population void-event information bound.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from a two-point Le Cam bound because the two ramp laws differ only when the rare arm is assigned.
seed_details.rebuttal: The full adaptive propensity log can itself differ across histories, so the shared subprobability measure and legal class membership must be established at experiment level; the exact constant and the separation from an HT limit are not supplied by generic Le Cam prose.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, the delayed-endpoint RTAR construction, the GUSTO-1 and EUROPA resampling analysis, Section 4 on drift, and the Discussion. The article reports post hoc resampling intervals; the first changed step is to condition on a prespecified bridge while retaining the assignment law and to allocate bridge error separately from atomic calibration error.
seed_details.opportunity: Give conditional finite-population coverage for delayed-endpoint RTAR under a prespecified expected-endpoint profile bridge.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A bridge-conditional version of the critical-law certificate with an explicit sensitivity allowance for bridge misspecification.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace stationarity-and-exchangeability resampling of patient pools by a fixed-potential-outcome sequential randomization law conditional on the prespecified bridge.
seed_details.destination_search: LiZhao2026 gives the nearest design-based framework and ChoBibautKallus2025 the nearest nonnormal simulation inversion; neither provides bridge-conditional bounded-hazard coverage.
seed_details.red_team: A direct specialization of LiZhao2026 once the expected endpoints are inserted as outcome regressions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Insertion alone does not verify the deterministic profile moduli over all counterfactual histories, and their Gaussian conditions do not cover bounded hazard; the application remains conditional until a bridge contract is established.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction, Algorithm 1, Theorem 1 and its proof in Appendix D, the Conclusion, and the limitations section. Their optimism argument yields asymptotic type-I control for specified bandit examples; the first changed step is to replace nuisance-biased trajectory simulation by a deterministic enclosure of every admissible signed critical law.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize when simulation-with-optimism and certified Poisson calibration agree and when atoms force divergent thresholds.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Derive an observable frontier in profile uncertainty and atom mass separating asymptotic equivalence of simulated and certified critical values from persistent threshold divergence.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace consistency of simulated nuisance laws with a quantitative Wasserstein-to-ramp bound uniform over the logged profile enclosure.
seed_details.destination_search: No source found an explicit atom-mass and profile-modulus frontier for adaptive simulation calibration.
seed_details.red_team: Routine from weak convergence plus Monte Carlo consistency.
seed_details.rebuttal: Weak convergence does not control discontinuous quantiles at atoms, so equivalence requires a derived smoothing and anti-discontinuity frontier; nevertheless the exact frontier is less directly supported than the selected seed.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the Introduction and desiderata, Theorem 1 with its test-martingale proof, fixed-time Corollary 1, and the Summary. Their wealth-process inversion is exact under predictable logging; the first changed step would be to replace a generic terminal boundary with a horizon-indexed compound-Poisson threshold while protecting every stopping time.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct an anytime-valid atom-safe confidence sequence whose terminal widths adapt to the critical intensity profile.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Combine a test-martingale safety layer with profile-specific Poisson terminal calibrations at a deterministic epoch grid.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The marginal critical-law transfer must be made simultaneous over epochs before Ville inversion can protect arbitrary stopping.
seed_details.destination_search: The Waudby-Smith et al. confidence sequences already give validity without bounded importance weights; no result found a sharp bounded-hazard compound-Poisson width guarantee.
seed_details.red_team: Generic confidence sequences already solve validity and any profile calibration is only a tuning improvement.
seed_details.rebuttal: The profile-specific atomic width could be new, but time-uniform protection may erase the proposed gain and the fixed-horizon consumer is more immediate.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the same source sections as for the honest-width seed, especially Section 4.3, where truncation materially changes finite-time width, and the Conclusion's design question.
seed_details.opportunity: Choose an exploration floor that minimizes certified rare-arm interval radius subject to a patient-benefit constraint.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A minimax allocation rule with a KKT or saddle certificate for the tradeoff between cumulative inferior-arm exposure and worst-case design-based radius.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Promote the truncation level from an inferential tuning choice to the design decision variable and derive a matching lower bound over feasible adaptive rules.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent adaptive-design work optimizes asymptotic variance or regret, but the present substrate does not yet supply a convex criterion for the atomic certified radius.
seed_details.red_team: A standard exploration-floor optimization once a variance formula is available.
seed_details.rebuttal: At bounded hazard the objective is an atomic profile quantile rather than variance, but no credible optimality certificate is yet visible, so the seed is dropped rather than padded.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read Theorem 4, the AIPW covariance discussion, Supplement S2.3, Section 6.3, and the Discussion. Their local efficiency language remains tied to Gaussian normalization; the first changed step is to define a bounded-hazard local experiment before asking for an efficiency bound.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the discontinuity between semiparametric Gaussian efficiency and finite-activity critical experiments.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A local asymptotic experiment showing where influence-function efficiency ceases to order procedures and a compound-Poisson decision bound replaces it.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace quadratic local asymptotic normality by convergence of likelihood ratios on the rare-assignment point process.
seed_details.destination_search: The available sources do not provide the required local likelihood for arbitrary finite populations, making the efficiency claim under-specified.
seed_details.red_team: Not well posed because fixed finite-population potential outcomes do not by themselves define differentiable local submodels.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds without an added local model, so this seed is dropped rather than assuming the information structure it seeks to derive.

seed_details.anchor_receipt: Read the multiarm setup in Section 2, Theorems 1 and 4, their martingale proofs, and the Discussion. The first changed step would couple several rare-arm indicators to a multivariate marked Poisson process under the simplex constraint.
seed_details.opportunity: Calibrate simultaneous contrasts when several arms have critical hazards.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A multivariate signed compound-Poisson transfer and simultaneous confidence region for a fixed contrast matrix.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace coordinatewise Bernoulli coupling by a categorical-to-Poisson coupling that preserves mutual exclusivity and cross-arm drift.
seed_details.destination_search: Multivariate Poisson approximation exists, but the extension from the binary kernel risks being a routine vectorization without a new frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Routine binary-to-fixed-\(K\) extension of the selected theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is presently persuasive because no new cross-arm sharpness or allocation frontier is identified, so the seed is dropped.

threads: LiZhao2026, Condition 3 and Theorem 4: design-based AIPW unbiasedness and Gaussian inference follow from a martingale decomposition, variance convergence, and Lindeberg; Section 6.3 displays undercoverage as the minimum probability decays faster.

BibautKallus2025, Sections 3, 6, and 7: the recent review isolates asymptotic negligibility and quadratic-variation convergence, then treats inversion of nonnormal adaptive laws as a distinct route whose construction remains incomplete beyond selected parametric and batched settings.

BarbourXia1999, Lemma 2.1 and Theorems 3.2 and 5.2: Stein perturbation and coupling yield explicit total-variation bounds for integer-valued compound-Poisson approximations; the real signed marks and predictable stopping in this project require a different transfer layer.

ChenEtAl2026, Proposition 2, Lemma 3, Theorem 6, and Section 8: independent Poisson importance sampling gives an exact compound-Poisson HT rate model and monotone bootstrap intervals, but not adaptive finite-population signed causal contrasts or uniform finite-experiment coverage.
literature_map.settled: Design-based martingale unbiasedness, Gaussian inference under Lindeberg, generic betting validity, and constant-profile Dickman limits are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_target_method_pair: No located result combines fixed finite populations, predictable \(1/t\)-scale rare assignment, real signed residual marks, completed-log profile enclosures, directed atomic convolution, and a finite error budget.
literature_map.subsumption_check: ChoBibautKallus2025 gives simulation-based asymptotic control under stochastic bandit examples, HongLeungLi2020 assumes a diverging effective sample size, and ChenEtAl2026 assumes independent Poisson importance sampling and studies a noncausal rate. None subsumes the kernel.

threads: FreidlingZhaoGao2026, Proposition 1 and Supplement S2: conditioning on assignments that reproduce the selected design gives selective type-I control for exact randomization tests.
WaudbySmithEtAl2024, Theorem 1: predictability of bets protects data-dependent logging and stopping, but a terminal profile-net selected from the completed log is not predictable.
CookMishlerRamdas2024, Theorem 1 and Section 4.3: propensity truncation preserves their asymptotic Gaussian theory and affects finite-time width, but does not calibrate discontinuous critical laws.
BarbourXia1999: distributional approximation errors can be explicit, but the paper does not address data-selected critical values.
literature_map.settled: Exact conditional selective randomization and predictable martingale selection are settled in their respective models.
literature_map.unoccupied_target_method_pair: The exact selection object here is an approximate law enclosure rather than an exact conditional randomization orbit; no closer paper provides the required deterministic monotone-threshold inclusion.
literature_map.subsumption_check: FreidlingZhaoGao2026 would subsume the claim only if conditioning on the completed log preserved the required randomization law, which it does not.

threads: CookMishlerRamdas2024 motivates lower bounds on adaptive interval width and studies how truncation changes width, but its main result is estimator-specific semiparametric Gaussian inference.
ShekharRamdas2023, equations (6)--(8): inverse information projections lower-bound width for i.i.d. bounded-mean confidence intervals and nearly characterize betting widths.
HongLeungLi2020 derives finite-population limited-overlap Gaussian inference when effective information diverges, leaving bounded hazard outside its asymptotic regime.
LiZhao2026 defines the complete finite-population adaptive randomization law needed to state an all-confidence-set comparison without a superpopulation surrogate.
literature_map.settled: Width lower bounds are known for i.i.d. bounded means and Gaussian limited-overlap regimes.
literature_map.unoccupied_target_method_pair: No located theorem uses the shared no-rare-assignment atom of two complete adaptive logged experiments to give the exact \(\sqrt{1/2}-0.1\) probability bound.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The i.i.d. information-projection bounds do not compare history-dependent propensity logs, and an HT limit cannot yield an arbitrary-confidence-set lower bound.

novelty_justification: The two closest inferential results are LiZhao2026 and WaudbySmithEtAl2024. The gap relative to Li and Zhao is coverage in a declared subset of their adaptive finite-population design framework that violates their Lindeberg route: \(e_{nt}\asymp\bar q(t/n)/t\) yields order-one rare-arm increments and an atomic signed compound-Poisson limit. Relative to Waudby-Smith et al., the advance is not generic validity but profile-specific finite-horizon radius: the completed log is converted into a simultaneous intensity enclosure, and every numerical, coupling, and threshold error is charged explicitly. FreidlingZhaoGao2026 protects exact post-selection randomization tests by conditioning; here completed-log conditioning is invalid for an approximate independent reference, so the new selection-safe move is deterministic threshold domination. ChenEtAl2026 is the closest newly located compound-Poisson HT collision, but its Poisson population size and independent importance draws make the compound-Poisson model exact; it provides neither a predictable adaptive transfer nor a signed finite-population ATE theorem. The all-set late-ramp lower bound is deliberately proved from a shared subprobability measure on the complete observation and is not inferred from the HT law. BarbourXia1999 and BhattacharjeeGoldstein2019 supply approximation and Dickman precedents but do not subsume adaptive signed-mark calibration.
